answer: A stake-bonded registry makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can trade, and the bond is slashed if peers prove it ran duplicate accounts. Like climbers sharing one summit rope, each identity carries real cost, so spinning up thousands of sock puppets means locking thousands of deposits. A light zephyr of random audits can trigger the slash, and a violet flag on a caught identity warns the whole market. Attackers pay per identity; honest agents pay once.
